display.title: Episode 229: Skippy and Crawly (Before Shavuos)
display.summary_short: Three days before Shavuos: a calculator shows how long ago the Torah was given, the march returns after Sefirah, and a father tells the tale of Skippy the grasshopper and Crawly the ant.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Gimmel Sivan, three days before Shavuos. With a calculator, Uncle Yossi subtracts the year of Matan Torah, 2448, from 5746 to show that the Torah was given 3,298 years ago, and explains the last days of counting the Omer. The Hakochainik march returns now that the days of Sefirah mourning are over. Uncle Yossi explains that Hashem gave the Torah because the children were our guarantors, and we renew 'Naaseh v'nishma'. A five-year-old girl says the Shema in Studio 604 and answers questions about brachos, followed by a sponsor message. The story is built on one of the Twelve Pesukim: 'I worked hard and succeeded, believe it'. Dovid asks his father why his sister Miriam gets better marks; she does her homework first, while he plays and does it tired at night. The father tells of Skippy the grasshopper, who hopped about all summer, and Crawly the ant, who stored food, so that in winter Skippy was left out in the cold. 'There was evening, and there was morning': hard work comes first, then success. The show closes with Chag Sameach and a reminder to hear the Ten Commandments in shul.
display.lesson: Work hard first and success will follow: 'I toiled and I found'. Prepare now, like the ant, instead of putting things off.

date.note: Confirmed by the audio: 'Today is Gimmel Sivan'; tonight is the 48th day of the Omer.
